newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods to look into selling stores.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods to look into selling stores.

text.p: Retailer and football pools group Littlewoods on Tuesday said it was reviewing its stores division and is looking into the possibility selling it.

"While we remain committed to generating higher returns from the stores business, we are also examining other strategic options. In particular, we have now determined to examine whether a disposal might realise greater shareholder value," chairman James Ross said in a statement.

Ross said the group would be focusing on its market-leading businesses in home shopping and leisure, where the company operates football pools. Littlewoods, controlled by the Moores family, also reported a 15 percent rise in profits for 1996 to 211.1 million pounds ($340.8 million) before tax, with sales down slightly to 2.28 billion pounds.

The 135-strong stores division had trading profit of 33.3 million pounds in 1996, virtually unchanged from 1995 before restructuring costs, on sales of 479 million. The company said the stores business was still not realising its full profit potential.

The Littlewoods statement gave no further details of the mooted sale of the division, but the Financial Times newspaper said its sale could bring the company substantially more than 500 million pounds.
Ross said trading in 1997 had started off encouragingly, with sales in its retail activities ahead by 5.1 percent in the first six weeks.
